body:
> Why did you choose components/**tests**/mycomponent.js over test/components/mycomponent.js?

So this is something I borrowed from the various famous react projects I looked at before doing our tests. Like react itself (https://github.com/facebook/react/tree/master/src/renderers/dom), react-router (https://github.com/rackt/react-router/tree/master/modules) and most rackt organization projects (https://github.com/rackt).

I found it handy and good because:
- tests are close to the implementation, in term of file organization
- you can cleary see if they are missing tests because if there's one missing test file then it's easier because there's less hierarchy to dig into
- we follow a convention that seems to get some traction in most react or not react based projects

It also look like what golang community is doing (file.go, file_test.go). Maybe we could directly take this road which is even better IMHO.

Good for you?
